name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SB2_Q01 - RCH programmes and their primary objectives in India

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In India, improved reproduction-related programmes covering wider areas are currently in operation under the name 'Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes'.

Statement II: Creating awareness about reproduction-related aspects and providing facilities and support for building a reproductively healthy society are major tasks under these programmes.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
India initiated national-level family planning programmes in 1951, which were periodically assessed and broadened over subsequent decades.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
The claim regarding the current programme name is correct: improved programmes covering wider reproduction-related areas operate under the popular name 'Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes'. The claim regarding their major tasks is also correct: creating awareness among people about various reproduction-related aspects and providing facilities and support for building a reproductively healthy society are central goals of RCH programmes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are factually accurate. Therefore, both the first and the second statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SB2_Q02 - Diagnostic use and legal status of amniocentesis

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Amniocentesis is used to test for the presence of genetic disorders such as Down syndrome, haemophilia, and sickle-cell anaemia in the developing foetus.

Statement II: In India, amniocentesis is legally permitted for determining the sex of the unborn child.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Amniocentesis involves analysing foetal cells and dissolved substances from amniotic fluid to assess genetic disorders and foetal survivability.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
The claim regarding genetic testing is correct because amniocentesis is used to detect disorders such as Down syndrome, haemophilia, and sickle-cell anaemia. However, the claim regarding sex-determination is incorrect because India has imposed a statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination to legally check the increasing menace of female foeticides.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The diagnostic description of amniocentesis is correct, whereas the claim about its legality for sex-determination is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SB2_Q03 - Periodic abstinence days and side effects of natural methods

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In the periodic abstinence method, couples avoid coitus from day 1 to day 7 of the menstrual cycle when ovulation is expected.

Statement II: Natural contraceptive methods have almost nil side effects because no medicines or devices are used, though their chances of failure are high.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Natural contraceptive methods aim to avoid the meeting of ovum and sperms without pharmacological or mechanical devices.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
The claim regarding the days of periodic abstinence is incorrect because couples must abstain from coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle (the fertile period when ovulation is expected), not day 1 to 7. The claim regarding side effects and failure rate is correct: because no medicines or devices are used, side effects are almost nil, though chances of failure are high.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement on the timing of periodic abstinence is incorrect, while the statement on side effects and failure rate of natural methods is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SB2_Q04 - Properties of condoms versus reusable cervical barriers

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Both male and female condoms are reusable rubber barriers that must be inserted by a doctor or expert nurse.

Statement II: Diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are disposable barriers that protect the user from contracting STIs and AIDS.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Barrier contraceptives differ in whether they are disposable or reusable, self-inserted or clinically placed, and whether they protect against STIs and AIDS.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
The claim about condoms is incorrect: both male and female condoms are disposable (not reusable) and can be self-inserted, giving privacy to the user. The claim about diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults is also incorrect: these rubber barriers are reusable (not disposable) and prevent conception by blocking sperm entry through the cervix, whereas protection against STIs and AIDS is a specific additional benefit of condoms.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements contain reversed and inaccurate descriptions, so both are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SB2_Q05 - Mechanisms of copper-releasing and hormone-releasing IUDs

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Copper-releasing IUDs such as CuT and Cu7 release copper ions that suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.

Statement II: Hormone-releasing IUDs such as Progestasert and LNG-20 make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs) increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus, while medicated IUDs provide additional copper-mediated or hormone-mediated contraceptive actions.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
The claim regarding copper-releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) is correct because the released copper ions suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity. The claim regarding hormone-releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20) is also correct because they additionally make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both mechanisms are accurately stated, so both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SB2_Q06 - Oral contraceptive pills and Saheli characteristics

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Oral contraceptive pills inhibit ovulation and implantation as well as alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent or retard sperm entry.

Statement II: 'Saheli' is a steroidal oral contraceptive pill that must be taken daily for 21 days followed by a 7-day gap.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Oral contraceptives prevent pregnancy by interfering with ovulation, implantation, and sperm transport, though conventional pills differ in composition and dosage schedule from Saheli.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
The claim about the mode of action of oral pills is correct: they inhibit ovulation and implantation and alter cervical mucus quality to prevent or retard sperm entry. However, the claim about Saheli is incorrect because Saheli contains a non-steroidal preparation and is a 'once a week' pill, not a daily steroidal pill.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement on the mechanism of oral pills is correct, whereas the statement on Saheli's composition and schedule is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SB2_Q07 - Reversibility of sterilisation and possible ill-effects of contraceptives

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Vasectomy and tubectomy are highly effective terminal methods of contraception with high reversibility.

Statement II: Contraceptives are not regular requirements for maintaining reproductive health, and their possible ill-effects include nausea, abdominal pain, breakthrough bleeding, irregular menstrual bleeding, or even breast cancer.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Surgical sterilisation methods are advised as terminal procedures, while contraceptive use in general must be weighed with qualified medical advice due to potential side effects.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
The claim regarding reversibility of vasectomy and tubectomy is incorrect because although these techniques are highly effective, their reversibility is very poor. The claim regarding contraceptive necessity and possible ill-effects is correct: contraceptives are practiced against a natural reproductive event rather than being regular requirements for reproductive health, and possible ill-effects such as nausea, abdominal pain, breakthrough bleeding, irregular menstrual bleeding, or even breast cancer should not be ignored.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement on reversibility of sterilisation is incorrect, while the statement on the role and possible ill-effects of contraceptives is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SB2_Q08 - Safety window and statutory opinion under MTP Amendment Act 2017

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Second trimester abortions are considered safer than first trimester Medical Terminations of Pregnancy (MTPs).

Statement II: Under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2017, a pregnancy lasting more than 12 weeks but fewer than 24 weeks can be terminated on the opinion of a single registered medical practitioner.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
MTP safety depends on gestational age, and the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017 establishes stricter medical oversight for later gestational stages.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
The claim regarding trimester safety is incorrect because MTPs are relatively safe during the first trimester (up to 12 weeks), whereas second trimester abortions are much riskier. The claim regarding practitioner opinion between 12 and 24 weeks is also incorrect because the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017 requires the opinion of two registered medical practitioners formed in good faith for pregnancies lasting more than 12 weeks but fewer than 24 weeks (one practitioner suffices only within the first 12 weeks).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements contradict the medical and legal provisions for MTP, so both are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SB2_Q09 - Curable versus incurable sexually transmitted infections

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Sexually transmitted infections such as gonorrhoea, syphilis, chlamydiasis, and trichomoniasis are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.

Statement II: Hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV infections are exceptions among common STIs because they are not completely curable.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Prompt diagnosis and treatment of STIs are key priorities under reproductive health-care programmes, though curability depends on the specific causative infection.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
Except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV infections, other common STIs such as gonorrhoea, syphilis, chlamydiasis, and trichomoniasis are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. Conversely, hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV infections are not completely curable.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both the claim regarding curable STIs and the claim regarding the three exceptions are accurate, so both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SB2_Q10 - IVF-ET and use of in-vivo fertilised embryos

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In Vitro Fertilisation followed by Embryo Transfer (IVF-ET) is popularly known as the 'test tube baby' programme.

Statement II: Embryos formed by in-vivo fertilisation cannot be used for embryo transfer to assist females who cannot conceive.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Embryo transfer (ET) techniques in assisted reproductive technology can utilise embryos generated either outside the body (in-vitro) or inside a female (in-vivo).

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
The claim regarding IVF-ET is correct: it is popularly known as the 'test tube baby' programme. However, the claim regarding in-vivo fertilisation is incorrect because embryos formed by in-vivo fertilisation (fusion of gametes within the female) can also be used for embryo transfer to assist females who cannot conceive.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement identifying IVF-ET as the test tube baby programme is correct, while the statement denying the use of in-vivo fertilised embryos is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SB2_Q11 - Distinction between ICSI and GIFT procedures

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI), semen collected from a healthy donor is artificially introduced into the vagina or uterus of the female.

Statement II: In Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer (GIFT), an ovum collected from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce an ovum, but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation and further development.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
ICSI, AI/IUI, and GIFT are distinct ART procedures tailored to different causes of infertility.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
The description attributed to ICSI is incorrect: introducing semen artificially into the vagina or uterus is Artificial Insemination (AI / IUI), whereas ICSI is a laboratory procedure in which a sperm is directly injected into the ovum to form an embryo. The description of GIFT is correct: a donor ovum is transferred into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce one, but can support fertilisation and further development.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement describing ICSI is incorrect, whereas the statement describing GIFT is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVE_HEALTH_SB2_Q12 - Spontaneous abortions and contraceptive acceptance in India

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Spontaneous abortions never occur in humans; all abortions are intentionally induced medical terminations of pregnancy.

Statement II: Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs) are rarely accepted in India, whereas oral contraceptive pills are the most widely used method among rural women.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Abortions can occur naturally as well as through medical induction, and contraceptive acceptance in India varies across methods.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Claims
The claim that spontaneous abortions never occur is incorrect: abortions can happen spontaneously as well, whereas intentional or voluntary termination before full term is specifically called medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) or induced abortion. The claim about contraceptive acceptance in India is also incorrect: IUDs are in fact one of the most widely accepted methods of contraception in India, whereas oral pills are not very popular among rural women.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are factually false, so both are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.
